media_work.title: Reasonable Doubt (48 Hours)
media_work.focus_or_theme: Questionable spousal murder conviction, prosecutorial misconduct, overturned conviction followed by reconviction.
media_work.summaryNotes: Case highlights how prosecutorial misconduct can overturn a conviction, but does not preclude retrial.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Questionable spousal murder conviction, prosecutorial misconduct, overturned conviction followed by reconviction.
media_item.summary_notes: Investigation into the controversial conviction that was later overturned due to prosecutorial misconduct, though Temple was later reconvicted at a new trial. The details accurately reflect his well-known case involving the murder of his wife, an overturned conviction due to prosecutorial misconduct (withholding evidence), and a subsequent reconviction in a later trial.

featured_individuals.time_served: Served ~9 years before first conviction overturned; currently incarcerated since 2019 reconviction.
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Convicted of the murder of his wife, Belinda Temple, in 1999. His first conviction was overturned in 2016 due to prosecutorial misconduct, but he was reconvicted in 2019 and is currently serving a life sentence.
contributing_factors_raw: Alleged prosecutorial misconduct (withholding favorable evidence - *Brady* violation)
